subject: maths
question: What is the SI unit of 'volume'?
solution:
The correct answer is __Cubic metre__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Volume__ is a measure of the amount of space an object occupies.
 
• The SI unit of volume is the cubic metre (m³).
 
• One cubic metre is the volume of a cube with sides of length 1 metre.
 
• Other common units for measuring volume include litres, millilitres, and cubic centimetres, but these are not SI units.
 
• 1 cubic metre is equivalent to 1000 litres.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Conversion Units:**

 
 
• 1 cubic metre = 1000 litres.
 
• 1 litre = 1000 millilitres.
 
• 1 cubic metre = 1,000,000 cubic centimetres.
 
 
 
• **Common Applications:**
 
 
• Measurement of liquid volumes in litres or millilitres.
 
• Measurement of large volumes in cubic metres, such as in construction or water reservoirs.
